findings.reason: clause (2) admits a passing run anywhere at or below ten times the forward solve, so for most passing bases the control cannot exceed the ceiling and the section's only falsifier never fires, which is the same constructed-outcome defect §2's clause (3) was repaired for.
findings.text: the negative control is "the same measurement with the reconstruction's convergence exit disabled and its iteration cap doubled", and that scaling only reaches the ceiling when the unmodified run already sits near it — with convergence exit disabled the control's wall is roughly (doubled cap / iterations used) times the base wall, so a base run measured at, say, 3× the forward solve rises to about 6× and stays under the 10× ceiling

findings.reason: a dispatch that honours the declaration will measure a cost the decision then changes, and the section either needs the deferred declaration §2 itself was given or a dependency scoped to the case-set work that does not turn on those decisions, so the author must choose which.
findings.text: §4 carries `data-status="implementable"` while its declared upstream §2 is `deferred` pending the `fitted-unknowns` and `vertical-freedom` decisions, and those decisions configure the very quantity §4 measures: what is fitted changes the unknown count and the iteration count, so the per-slice wall and the ratio to the forward solve are measured for a configuration the plan has not yet fixed
